segments.t: Following the voice into the walk-in cooler, Kristina unties the freezing captive and reveals to a stunned Nagiyev that the man is not a journalist at all, but the private detective she hired to follow him. Nagiyev immediately blames Senya and Fedya while trying to appease his wife.
Наняли частного детектива следить за мной?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'And what are you doing in here?' Nastya tests bluntly about what Nagiyev just brought up.

'That was not part of our deal.' Nagiyev chimes in plainly around Nastya and reaches for the Russian word "dogovarivalis" ("had an agreement", built from "dogovarivatsya") right at the center of the line.
'I thought so.' Opening up directly right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I do not understand.' Nagiyev fires back at once facing Kristina, watching Kristina's face to see how the news lands.
'Wait, do you know this weirdo?' Emphasizing the oddball in this beat, Nagiyev puts the weight on "chudaka" ("oddball", from "chudak") as the exchange unfolds.
'Ah, so that is what this is about.' Holding firm earnestly at once, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Наняли частного детектива следить за мной?
'You hired a private detective to spy on me?' Nastya quizzes straight out while looking straight at Nagiyev here.
'I thought he was a journalist.' Pointing to a journalist right here, Nagiyev leans on "zhurnalist" ("journalist") to give the whole sentence its punch.

'Not me personally, of course.' Kristina quietly shares this confirmation at this moment using "konechno" ("of course") — spoken with a soft "shn" sound in everyday Moscow Russian to mean "of course, certainly".
'These handsome guys right here did it.' Nastya opens up pointedly facing Kristina, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'I will sort everything out right now.' Nagiyev reacts dryly to Nastya and reaches for the Russian word "reshu" ("I'll solve", built from "reshit") right at the center of the line.
'I certainly hope so.' Holding firm warmly before Nagiyev, the "-sya" ending on "nadeyus" ("hope so") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'I already told you.' Nastya opens up earnestly toward Kristina, to clear the air between them once and for all.
Наняли частного детектива следить за мной?

That wraps up this scene as kristina opens the walk-in cooler and reveals that the bound man is actually the private detective she hired to spy on Nagiyev, turning the tables on her husband. See you next time!
